items.syntax: col IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
items.explanation: Comparisons with NULL return NULL, never true.
items.example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE employee_id IS NULL;
SELECT order_id, COALESCE(shipped_date::text, 'not shipped') AS shipped FROM orders ORDER BY shipped_date NULLS FIRST LIMIT 5;

items.explanation: NULL when a = b; classic guard against division by zero.
items.example: SELECT product_name, ROUND(unit_price / NULLIF(units_on_order, 0), 2) AS ratio FROM products LIMIT 5;
items.expected: Ratio is NULL because units_on_order is 0.

items.explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) counts non-NULL values.
items.example: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders, COUNT(shipped_date) AS shipped, COUNT(employee_id) AS with_employee FROM orders;

items.syntax: ORDER BY col DESC NULLS LAST
items.explanation: PostgreSQL sorts NULLs as largest: last in ASC, first in DESC.
items.example: SELECT order_id, shipped_date FROM orders ORDER BY shipped_date DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5;
items.expected: Latest shipped orders, NULLs at the end.

items.explanation: Treats two NULLs as equal and NULL vs value as different.
items.example: SELECT order_id, employee_id FROM orders WHERE employee_id IS DISTINCT FROM 1 LIMIT 5;
items.expected: Orders not by employee 1, including the NULL one.

items.explanation: One NULL in the list makes NOT IN return no rows; use NOT EXISTS.
items.example: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_returned FROM employees WHERE employee_id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM orders);

items.explanation: AVG divides by the count of non-NULL values; SUM of no rows is NULL.
items.example: SELECT SUM(freight) FILTER (WHERE freight < 0) AS sum_none, COALESCE(SUM(freight) FILTER (WHERE freight < 0), 0) AS sum_zero FROM orders;
